title: Kept: Jeremiah 33-35, Ecclesiastes 10, John 4, 1 Peter 1
summary: Pilot episode, about ten minutes, built around the word 'kept.' Jeremiah 33: God's call to prayer from prison, the righteous Branch and the name 'The Lord is our righteousness,' and the covenant with David and Levi tied to day and night. Jeremiah 34: Zedekiah warned; the slave-release covenant broken once the siege lifted, the calf cut in two, contrasted with Genesis 15. Jeremiah 35: the Rechabites' obedience to Jonadab versus Judah's disobedience, and the promise that Jonadab will never lack a man to stand before God (not a teetotal mandate; Christian liberty). Ecclesiastes 10: dead flies, sharpening the dull iron (v. 10), the sagging roof, the bird that carries your words. John 4: the woman leaves her jar; shame turned to testimony; 'my food is to do the will of him who sent me.' 1 Peter 1:1-9: elect exiles, living hope, an inheritance kept and believers guarded, faith tested like gold.
threads: Jeremiah 35 was covered only briefly; the next Jeremiah episode can deepen it and then move into Jeremiah 36-38 (the scroll burned, Jeremiah in the cistern).
The 'never lack a man' promises link Jeremiah 33:17-18 and 35:19.
Ecclesiastes is heading toward its close in chapters 11-12.
1 Peter's theme of exile and the scattered people of God echoes Jeremiah's exile setting.

The pilot leaned on New Testament fulfillment in every section; the listener asked for future episodes to stay in each passage and its commentary, using the New Testament only where the text warrants.
show_notes: Pilot episode. Shorter and more devotional than the regular format.
